summary: This excerpt from Book 1 (part 171) is a fiction passage in which the narrator Marcus is caught in an alley scene. Masha, who reveals she is with DHS, confronts a pale young man named Charles, handcuffs him after he tried to help, and then knocks Marcus down when he runs. She forces him to a moving van on a Nob Hill side street, labeled Three Guys and a Truck Moving, where an older black man lets them in. The passage is mainly action and tension, with Masha controlling the situation.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, Masha of DHS arrests Charles in an alley, tackles the fleeing Marcus, and leads him to a moving van on Nob Hill.
key_facts: Masha identifies herself as DHS, saying 'DHS, dick-head,' and shows a wallet to prove it.
Masha accuses Charles of 'Obstruction of National Security' after he interfered with her pursuit.
Charles protests 'I was trying to help!' before Masha twists him into a judo hold and cuffs him with a plastic handcuff strip.
Marcus runs down the alley but is tackled from behind by Masha and falls face-first onto grimy asphalt.
Marcus has a hurt foot and is carrying a heavy pack, which slows his escape.
Masha had earlier put Marcus in a judo hold back at Civic Center.
Masha says she has been running Marcus back to his masters to see where he went.
The vehicle is a sixteen-wheeler moving van on a Nob Hill side-street, marked 'Three Guys and a Truck Moving.'
The moving van is parked outside a tall apartment building with a green awning.
An older black guy with a kidney-belt and heavy gloves watches the van and smiles at Masha and Marcus.
The man tells them 'Under the big table,' directing them inside the truck.
Masha says 'Come on, it's not far now' as she leads Marcus onward.
Marcus says he hurt all over and wanted to die after the fall.
